changes.before: Change the index vector to c(2,3). What prints?
changes.after: A positive index tells R which position to take. The first position is one.

before: values[1] selects the first element, not the second. Brackets request a subset.
values[c(1,3)] selects the first and third entries, in that requested order. Repeating an index can repeat an entry.
For this simple atomic vector, an absent positive position yields NA. Other extraction operators have different rules, taught later.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
values <- c(10, 20, 30)
cat(values[c(1, 3)], sep=",")
```
Expected output or behavior: 10,30. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Map each requested position to its selected value before running the expression. You may trace it without a R interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

The index vector can ask for several positions in one step.
Keep the values from the requested positions, in the requested order.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
values <- c(10, 20, 30)
cat(values[c(1, 3)], sep=",")
```
The output is `10,30`. Positions one and three hold ten and thirty.
Choose positions two and three instead.
